issues.reason: Names and casing requires the kind to be stated in one ordinary type atom "whether the kind word sits inside the name or beside it" — the Kestrel River example emits (Member kestrel_river river) alongside the Name — so (Member standard_and_poors_500_index index) is missing.

Goal is the spatial non-recipient "to" oblique (motion-result path), and an oblique's object follows the ordinary NP rules, so a bare float in the filler slot is ill-typed — numbers are magnitudes in Measure / Cardinality / Ordinal, never role fillers.

The scale rule's second branch is precisely a dimension noun read off the measure verb ("weighs" → weight, "costs" → price), and fall is the surface verb's own noun with no gradable adjective stated, so the parse records what's said rather than substituting a synonym.

gaps_confirmed: A parenthetical ticker / secondary identifier ("<.SPX>"): exactly one Name fact per proper noun, with no slot for an alternate code.
Appositive / restatement "or" ("0.70 points, or 0.07 percent" — one change re-expressed in another unit), which the Disjunction section would treat as inclusive disjunction.
The resulting numeric value of a change-of-value verb ("fell … to 1,069.42"): no licensed endpoint-value encoding (Measure needs a unit, Goal is spatial).
new_gaps: A bare numeric value has no licensed filler form for a role or preposition-named oblique slot, so an endpoint value cannot be attached to its event even with the surface preposition head (To).
Two Measure atoms sharing an entity and scale but differing in unit (point vs percent) express one quantity two ways, and neither unit has a canonical-dimension conversion to reconcile them.
repair_summary: Added (: idx_type (Member standard_and_poors_500_index index) (STV 1.0 0.99)) for the kind word inside the name run; removed (Goal sk_fall_1 1069.42), whose numeric filler has no licensed replacement, and recorded the endpoint-value gap.
notes: The endpoint is dropped rather than re-slotted, since a Measure would need an invented scale and the To oblique would still take a bare number. Reading the two magnitudes as one fall measured twice, not an (Or …), keeps every atom true and is left untouched.
